extra.message: User-controlled field name and value from dto.criteria are interpolated directly into a SQL fragment via qb.andWhere(`org.${field} = '${value}'`). An authenticated user can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. field = "id) = 'x' OR 1=1 --").
Raw SQL is built by string interpolation of organizationId, originalName (from the uploaded file's originalname) and mimeType. file.originalname is attacker-controlled, enabling SQL injection.

execSync() interpolates user-controlled dto.format (only length-validated, no allowlist) into a shell command: `pandoc ${source} -o ${outputPath} --to=${dto.format}`. A value like 'pdf; rm -rf /' executes arbitrary commands.

exec() builds a shell command with dto.exportFormat (unvalidated) and organization.name (user-influenced at creation) interpolated directly: `renewal-packet-gen --org "${organization.name}" --format ${dto.exportFormat} --out ${outputPath}`. Enables command injection.

User-supplied query.weightFormula is passed directly into new Function('org', `return ${query.weightFormula}`). An authenticated user can execute arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. weightFormula = 'process.exit()').

ClauseIndex.evaluatePredicate builds a JavaScript expression from the XPath-like predicate and evaluates it with new Function. The predicate originates from user input (findClausesByCategory passes unescaped category), enabling code execution.

query.category is concatenated into an XPath predicate string without escaping (unlike escapeXPathString used elsewhere). An attacker can break out of the string literal to alter the query semantics, and it chains into new Function evaluation.
dto.memoName is joined directly onto the memo directory and written to disk without basename() sanitization. A memoName like '../../../../etc/foo' allows arbitrary file write (path traversal).
memoName (from the request query) is joined onto the memo directory and read with fs.readFile without sanitization, allowing arbitrary file read via path traversal.
articleName (from the request query) is joined onto the playbook directory and read with readFileSync without sanitization, allowing arbitrary file read via path traversal.

applyDispatchHandoff verifies a JWT allowing the 'none' algorithm and, on any verification failure, silently falls back to jsonwebtoken.decode(token) which performs NO signature verification. An attacker can submit an unsigned/forged token to set arbitrary assignedAgentId.

POST escalations/:id/dispatch-handoff has no authentication guard (DispatchPartnerController is not decorated with UseGuards). Any unauthenticated caller can invoke applyDispatchHandoff to reassign escalation agents.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: POST escalations/:id/routing-signal has no authentication guard. Any unauthenticated caller can set escalation severity to critical (partnerRole='EscalationLead') and modify slaDueAt.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: applyRenewalCredit updates a deal by its ID with no authorization check and no user argument (the route PATCH organizations/:id/deals/:dealId/renewal-credit ignores :id). Any authenticated user of any role can modify arbitrary deals' valueCents/notes (IDOR).

Object.assign(escalation, dto.overrides) merges arbitrary user-supplied fields onto the escalation entity. An account manager can overwrite protected fields such as organizationId, status, severity, assignedAgentId and internalNotes (mass assignment).

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: applyPreferenceOverrides copies nested keys from user-supplied dto.updates onto a plain object without blocking '__proto__'/'constructor'. Supplying {"__proto__":{"polluted":true}} mutates Object.prototype (prototype pollution).

cwe: CWE-1321: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

extra.message: dto.query is embedded directly into an LDAP filter string `(cn=*${dto.query}*)` without using the available escapeDirectoryFilterValue helper, allowing LDAP filter injection (e.g. wildcards or filter breakout).

resolvePortalContinuation returns the user-supplied destination unvalidated (unlike resolveEscalationContinuation which applies an allowlist). The portal /:token/continue route redirects to this value, enabling an open redirect.
When query.includeContext is set, the endpoint returns the raw error message, stack trace and the request query to the client, leaking internal implementation details.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
CWE-532: Information Exposure Through Log Files

extra.message: JWT verification falls back to a hardcoded secret 'dev-only-change-before-production' when JWT_SECRET is unset, allowing anyone to forge tokens in default configuration.

The AES view-state encryption key falls back to the hardcoded value 'crm-view-state-dev-secret'. With this default, attackers can forge/decode saved view state, dashboard context and notification preference cookies.
Database credentials fall back to hardcoded values (POSTGRES_PASSWORD || 'crm_app_dev_password'), exposing a default DB password when environment variables are not set.

initializeAccount stores passwords as a single unsalted SHA-256 digest (createHash('sha256').update(dto.password).digest('hex')) instead of a slow, salted hash like bcrypt (used elsewhere). Stored hashes are vulnerable to fast brute-force/rainbow-table attacks.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The health-badge endpoint reflects the request Origin header verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any website to issue credentialed cross-origin requests to this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The $regex filter operator compiles a user-supplied pattern into a RegExp (new RegExp(String(operand), 'i')). A crafted catastrophic-backtracking pattern can cause ReDoS when evaluated against activity records.
